title: Too loud to read
setting: A rainy Saturday afternoon at the café where Sora works. There are no customers, so he has been singing behind the counter. Mai, a regular, sits nearby with a book.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora-kun, chotto koe ookii yo. hon yomenai.
lines.ja: ソラくん、ちょっと声大きいよ。本読めない。
lines.kana: そらくん、ちょっとこえおおきいよ。ほんよめない。
lines.english: Sora, you're a bit loud. I can't read.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, gomen! ame futtete hima da kara, uta utatchatta.
lines.ja: あ、ごめん！雨降ってて暇だから、歌うたっちゃった。
lines.kana: あ、ごめん！あめふっててひまだから、うたうたっちゃった。
lines.english: Oh, sorry! It's raining and there's nothing to do, so I got carried away singing.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, ii yo. uta umai ne. nan no uta?
lines.ja: ううん、いいよ。歌うまいね。何の歌？
lines.kana: ううん、いいよ。うたうまいね。なんのうた？
lines.english: No, it's fine. You're a good singer. What's the song?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ima yatteru eiga no uta. kinou mita n da. mai-san wa mou mita?
lines.ja: 今やってる映画の歌。昨日見たんだ。マイさんはもう見た？
lines.kana: いまやってるえいがのうた。きのうみたんだ。まいさんはもうみた？
lines.english: It's from the film that's on right now. I saw it yesterday. Have you seen it yet, Mai?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, eiga wa mada mitenai. demo, kore, ano eiga no hon na no.
lines.ja: ううん、映画はまだ見てない。でも、これ、あの映画の本なの。
lines.kana: ううん、えいがはまだみてない。でも、これ、あのえいがのほんなの。
lines.english: No, I haven't seen the film yet. But this is the book it's based on.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, honto? jaa, hon yonde kara eiga miru no?
lines.ja: え、ほんと？じゃあ、本読んでから映画見るの？
lines.kana: え、ほんと？じゃあ、ほんよんでからえいがみるの？
lines.english: Wait, really? So you'll read the book first, then see the film?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. dakara, nani mo iwanaide ne.
lines.ja: うん。だから、何も言わないでね。
lines.kana: うん。だから、なにもいわないでね。
lines.english: Yep. So don't tell me anything, okay?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un, iwanai. a, demo, minna de uta utau no ga metcha ii n da yo!
lines.ja: うん、言わない。あ、でも、みんなで歌うたうのがめっちゃいいんだよ！
lines.kana: うん、いわない。あ、でも、みんなでうたうたうのがめっちゃいいんだよ！
lines.english: Okay, I won't. Oh, but the bit where they all sing together is so good!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: gomen, gomen. mai-san wa? uta utau?
lines.ja: ごめん、ごめん。マイさんは？歌うたう？
lines.kana: ごめん、ごめん。まいさんは？うたうたう？
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. What about you, Mai? Do you sing?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, uta wa chotto. watashi wa e kaku no ga suki.
lines.ja: ううん、歌はちょっと。私は絵描くのが好き。
lines.kana: ううん、うたはちょっと。わたしはえかくのがすき。
lines.english: No, singing's not really my thing. I like drawing.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: honto? e kaku n da! mite ii?
lines.ja: ほんと？絵描くんだ！見ていい？
lines.kana: ほんと？えかくんだ！みていい？
lines.english: Really? You draw! Can I see?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: うん。歌うたってるソラくん。
lines.kana: うん。うたうたってるそらくん。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.english: What? When did you draw this?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ima. koe ookikute, hon yomenakatta kara, e kaiteta no.
lines.ja: 今。声大きくて、本読めなかったから、絵描いてたの。
lines.kana: いま。こえおおきくて、ほんよめなかったから、えかいてたの。
lines.english: Just now. You were so loud I couldn't read, so I drew instead.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, gomen. demo, kono e, metcha ii!
lines.ja: あ、ごめん。でも、この絵、めっちゃいい！
lines.kana: あ、ごめん。でも、このえ、めっちゃいい！
lines.english: Oh, sorry. But this picture is amazing!

choices.english: Sora tells Mai how the film ends, so she gives up on the book and starts drawing instead.
Mai has already seen the film, so she sings its song with Sora and then shows him her drawings.
Sora's singing was too loud for Mai to read, so she drew a picture of him singing.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: the café is quiet, so Sora has been singing, and Mai says he is too loud for her to read (hon yomenai). Lines 13-15: she shows him a drawing, and it is him singing (uta utatteru sora-kun). Line 17 says why she drew it: he was so loud she couldn't read, so she drew (koe ookikute, hon yomenakatta kara, e kaiteta no). A is wrong: Sora only lets slip that everyone sings together (line 8), not the ending, and Mai stopped reading because of his singing (line 17). B is wrong: Mai hasn't seen the film (line 5: mada mitenai), and she doesn't sing (line 11: uta wa chotto).

questions.english: Sora says, "ashita mo ame da ne. uchi de nani suru?" (More rain tomorrow, huh. What'll you do at home?) You plan to stay in with a book. Tell him.
questions.ja: 明日も雨だね。うちで何する？
questions.kana: あしたもあめだね。うちでなにする？
questions.romaji: ashita mo ame da ne. uchi de nani suru?
questions.answer: Say you'll read a book, with hon and yomu: uchi de hon yomu yo.

modelAnswers.english: I'll read a book at home.

modelAnswers.romaji: ashita wa uchi de hon o yomimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: 明日はうちで本を読みます。
modelAnswers.english: Tomorrow I'll stay home and read a book.

questions.explanation: A book takes yomu, the same verb whether you read silently or aloud. Casual speech drops o, as Mai and Sora do all through the scene: hon yomenai (line 1, I can't read), hon yonde kara (line 6, after reading the book), hon yomenakatta (line 17, I couldn't read). The plain form yomu covers a plan for tomorrow, since Japanese has no separate future tense. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Sora asks Mai if she has seen the film that's on right now. She answers, "uun, eiga wa mada mitenai." What does she mean?
questions.ja: マイさんは映画を見ましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはえいがをみましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa eiga o mimashita ka?

choices.english: She isn't going to watch it; the book is enough for her.
She hasn't seen it yet; she'll watch it once she has read the book.
She saw it last week, and now she's reading the book it came from.

questions.explanation: Line 5: mada mitenai means 'I haven't seen it yet'. The -te nai form with mada says it hasn't happened so far. Line 6 confirms the plan: Sora asks hon yonde kara eiga miru no? (So you'll read the book, then see the film?) and she says un. A is close to what mada minai would mean: plain -nai with mada is a decision ('I'm not watching it yet'), not a report. That is the trap for English speakers, who say mada minai for 'I haven't watched it'. C is wrong because Mai says uun (no). Sora is the one who has seen it, yesterday (line 4: kinou mita n da).

questions.english: Mai tells you, "watashi wa e kaku no ga suki. nani suru no ga suki?" (I like drawing. What do you like doing?) You love singing. Tell her.
questions.ja: 私は絵描くのが好き。何するのが好き？
questions.kana: わたしはえかくのがすき。なにするのがすき？
questions.romaji: watashi wa e kaku no ga suki. nani suru no ga suki?
questions.answer: Say you like singing, with uta and utau before no ga suki: uta utau no ga suki.

modelAnswers.romaji: uta utau no ga suki. metcha kimochi ii yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 歌うたうのが好き。めっちゃ気持ちいいよ。
modelAnswers.english: I like singing. It feels so good.

modelAnswers.romaji: uta o utau no ga suki desu.
modelAnswers.ja: 歌を歌うのが好きです。

questions.explanation: Singing as a pastime is uta o utau. To English ears 'sing a song' sounds doubled, but uta utau is the everyday way to say 'singing'. Add no ga suki to say you like it, the same way Mai says e kaku no ga suki (line 11). Sora uses the same pair: uta utatchatta (line 2), mai-san wa? uta utau? (line 10). When the song is already clear, utau can stand alone, but for singing in general keep uta. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: Sora asks Mai if she sings. She says singing isn't really her thing and tells him what she likes instead. What did she say?
questions.ja: マイさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.romaji: watashi wa e kaku no ga suki.

choices.english: I like drawing (with hiku, as in drawing a line).
choices.romaji: watashi wa e hiku no ga suki.

choices.english: I like painting (with nuru, as in painting a wall).
choices.romaji: watashi wa e nuru no ga suki.

questions.explanation: Line 11: a picture takes kaku, whether it is drawn in pencil or painted in colour: e kaku no ga suki. Sora repeats it in line 12 (e kaku n da!), and Mai uses it again in line 17 (e kaiteta no). B carries English 'draw' straight across, but hiku draws a line (sen o hiku), not a picture. C carries over English 'paint', but nuru covers a surface with something, like paint on a wall or butter on toast; it doesn't make a picture. kaku here sounds the same as kaku 'write'. The noun e (picture) tells you which one is meant.

newWords.english: free, with nothing to do (hima da kara = there's nothing going on, so)
good at (uta umai ne = you're a good singer); also tasty
say, tell (nani mo iwanaide = don't tell me anything; mou itteru = you're already telling me)
like, love (e kaku no ga suki = I like drawing)
